title: Seasonal shape terms increase median test error in 80 selected LINEAR RRab stars
abstract: We test seasonal amplitude and phase terms in 80 bright, frequently observed LINEAR RRab stars. A fixed Fourier shape and a seasonal shape model are fitted on alternate observing nights and tested on the other nights. Seasonal terms increase median weighted squared error by 16.3 percent, with a conditional interval from 8.7 to 20.9 percent. Exchanging the night sets gives an 11.0 percent increase. Four first-split leads retain positive gains in the reverse split, but only two retain gains after a quadratic phase term is added to the baseline. A public ZTF query for the strongest initial lead does not meet the coverage rule for the same seasonal test. The result limits this prediction method for this selected sample. It does not exclude pulsation modulation or establish a new signal. We include code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Full test-score distributions and sensitivity to the Fourier harmonic order. Positive scores mean lower test error. Stationary Gaussian controls use the observed sampling and a restricted local frequency search.

citations.reason: Related pulsation-phase test in a different RR Lyrae star and survey. No data or code are reused.
